Kentucky context: the state is split among four grids. East Kentucky Power Cooperative, Kentucky Power (an AEP company) and Duke Energy Kentucky are in PJM; Big Rivers Electric is in MISO and Owensboro Municipal Utilities joins MISO in 2027; LG&E and KU (PPL companies) run their own balancing authority outside any market; TVA's Marshall, Paradise and Shawnee plants are federal and outside any market and outside Kentucky PSC jurisdiction. The Kentucky Public Service Commission hears certificates of public convenience and necessity, IRPs and rate cases for LG&E, KU, Kentucky Power, Duke Energy Kentucky, EKPC and Big Rivers; its case filings are open PDFs (psc.ky.gov/pscecf/<case>/...) and its orders sit at psc.ky.gov/pscscf/<year> Cases/<case>/. The harvest file batches/us-ky/harvest/psc_dockets.md lists the cases found for every plant. Air permits come from two agencies: the Kentucky Division for Air Quality for most of the state and the Louisville Metro Air Pollution Control District for Jefferson County (Mill Creek, Cane Run, Paddys Run). The permit harvest is in scopes/us-ky/work/permits/<plant_id>.md. Municipal and cooperative utilities (KYMEA, Paducah Power, Owensboro Municipal Utilities, EKPC's members) do not file for a certificate at the commission; their record is the air permit, the queue, their board minutes and their own reports. This batch is staged for Baird's own review page; no colleague's edits are a baseline in Kentucky.

Integrated resource plans, all on the commission's site: Kentucky Power 2022 IRP (case 2023-00092; the preferred plan adds 480 MW of gas turbines in 2029 after the Mitchell coal exit; next IRP due March 20, 2027), Duke Energy Kentucky 2024 IRP (case 2024-00197; East Bend diesel co-firing in 2030 and a new combined cycle unit in 2039) and the Duke Energy Kentucky 2026 IRP (case 2026-00167, filed 2026; it replaces the 2024 plan for East Bend), EKPC 2025 IRP (case 2025-00087; Liberty Station 214 MW engines, Cooper CC1 745/800 MW, Cooper 2 gas up to 100 percent, Spurlock 1 to 4 co-firing up to 50 percent), LG&E/KU 2024 IRP (case 2024-00326; Mill Creek 5 in 2027, Brown 12 in 2030 and Mill Creek 6 in 2031 for data center load; next IRP October 19, 2027), Big Rivers 2023 IRP (case 2023-00310; Green Station retirement 2029 and a 635 MW combined cycle in June 2029) and the Big Rivers 2026 IRP (case 2026-00268, filed September 2026, filings through October 30, 2026; it replaces the 2023 plan for every Big Rivers plant and the placeholder), KYMEA 2023 IRP (kymea.org; no gas beyond Energy Center I), and TVA's 2026 IRP (tva.com; the 2025 draft was never finalized). For every plant check the plan for a start date, a retirement year or a capacity that disagrees with the export, cite the PDF page, and give the reviewer an IRP Notes line.

Start years on converted units: Big Sandy 1, Green Station 1 and 2, Robert Reid 1 and the Cooper and Spurlock timepoint 2 rows carry the gas conversion year or planned conversion year, while the EIA-860M file carries the original unit's operating year (1963, 1979, 1981, 1976). Kentucky context: the state is split among four grids. East Kentucky Power Cooperative, Kentucky Power (an AEP company) and Duke Energy Kentucky are in PJM; Big Rivers Electric is in MISO and Owensboro Municipal Utilities joins MISO in 2027; LG&E and KU (PPL companies) run their own balancing authority outside any market; TVA's Marshall, Paradise and Shawnee plants are federal and outside any market and outside Kentucky PSC jurisdiction. The Kentucky Public Service Commission hears certificates of public convenience and necessity, IRPs and rate cases for LG&E, KU, Kentucky Power, Duke Energy Kentucky, EKPC and Big Rivers; its case filings are open PDFs (psc.ky.gov/pscecf/<case>/...) and its orders sit at psc.ky.gov/pscscf/<year> Cases/<case>/. The harvest file batches/us-ky/harvest/psc_dockets.md lists the cases found for every plant. Air permits come from two agencies: the Kentucky Division for Air Quality for most of the state and the Louisville Metro Air Pollution Control District for Jefferson County (Mill Creek, Cane Run, Paddys Run). The permit harvest is in scopes/us-ky/work/permits/<plant_id>.md. Municipal and cooperative utilities (KYMEA, Paducah Power, Owensboro Municipal Utilities, EKPC's members) do not file for a certificate at the commission; their record is the air permit, the queue, their board minutes and their own reports. This batch is staged for Baird's own review page; no colleague's edits are a baseline in Kentucky.

Kentucky context: the state is split among four grids. East Kentucky Power Cooperative, Kentucky Power (an AEP company) and Duke Energy Kentucky are in PJM; Big Rivers Electric is in MISO and Owensboro Municipal Utilities joins MISO in 2027; LG&E and KU (PPL companies) run their own balancing authority outside any market; TVA's Marshall, Paradise and Shawnee plants are federal and outside any market and outside Kentucky PSC jurisdiction. The harvest file batches/us-ky/harvest/psc_dockets.md lists the cases found for every plant. Air permits come from two agencies: the Kentucky Division for Air Quality for most of the state and the Louisville Metro Air Pollution Control District for Jefferson County (Mill Creek, Cane Run, Paddys Run). The permit harvest is in scopes/us-ky/work/permits/<plant_id>.md. Municipal and cooperative utilities (KYMEA, Paducah Power, Owensboro Municipal Utilities, EKPC's members) do not file for a certificate at the commission; their record is the air permit, the queue, their board minutes and their own reports. Kentucky context: the state is split among four grids. East Kentucky Power Cooperative, Kentucky Power (an AEP company) and Duke Energy Kentucky are in PJM; Big Rivers Electric is in MISO and Owensboro Municipal Utilities joins MISO in 2027; LG&E and KU (PPL companies) run their own balancing authority outside any market; TVA's Marshall, Paradise and Shawnee plants are federal and outside any market and outside Kentucky PSC jurisdiction. The Kentucky Public Service Commission hears certificates of public convenience and necessity, IRPs and rate cases for LG&E, KU, Kentucky Power, Duke Energy Kentucky, EKPC and Big Rivers; its case filings are open PDFs (psc.ky.gov/pscecf/<case>/...) and its orders sit at psc.ky.gov/pscscf/<year> Cases/<case>/. The harvest file batches/us-ky/harvest/psc_dockets.md lists the cases found for every plant. Air permits come from two agencies: the Kentucky Division for Air Quality for most of the state and the Louisville Metro Air Pollution Control District for Jefferson County (Mill Creek, Cane Run, Paddys Run). The permit harvest is in scopes/us-ky/work/permits/<plant_id>.md. Municipal and cooperative utilities (KYMEA, Paducah Power, Owensboro Municipal Utilities, EKPC's members) do not file for a certificate at the commission; their record is the air permit, the queue, their board minutes and their own reports. This batch is staged for Baird's own review page; no colleague's edits are a baseline in Kentucky.
